function: Learned joint choice of LED-array transmit beamforming, LED selection, RSMA rate adaptation and ORIS element association to maximize energy efficiency (pp. 8-9).
system: Indoor 8x8x3 m optical MISO downlink: 16 LEDs, 4 single-PD users, fixed wall-mounted reflecting ORIS (16-256 elements swept); LED optical band, RSMA with SLIPT (pp. 4, 12, 14).
method: Meta-PPO: proximal policy optimization actor-critic (continuous and discrete actions) with meta-learning over user-location tasks plus a meta-adaptation phase; reinforcement learning, trained online (pp. 8-12).
data_channel: Custom indoor simulator: Lambertian LoS and ORIS NLoS optical channels, random user positions in an 8x8x3 m room; no dataset or measurements (pp. 5-6, 12).
test_conditions: Meta-training over tasks of user locations, then meta-adaptation; sweeps of users, power, dimming, LEDs, ORIS size; the unseen test scenario and adaptation effort are not stated (pp. 10-14).
baselines: Non-learned: convex optimization, random ORIS association, no ORIS, NOMA variant; learned: PPO without meta-learning (pp. 12-14).
metrics: Energy efficiency (bits/J/Hz) versus episodes, users, maximum power, QoS, harvesting threshold, dimming level, LEDs and ORIS elements (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Training and running complexity orders as layer-size products times tasks, episodes and steps (Eqs. 50-51); no FLOPs or runtime reported (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 5: "The Lambertian model is considered to determine the direct LoS channel gain"; custom Lambertian LoS and ORIS NLoS optical simulator (Eqs. 3, 11) with the room set-up on p. 12. No standardized or measured channel is used, so it is missing.
q2_support: p. 10: "locations for each user determines each task"; a meta-adaptation phase is defined (Algorithm 2, p. 12) but no test in an unseen scenario and no adaptation effort are reported, and the sweeps (pp. 13-14) only vary users, power, dimming, LEDs and ORIS size.
q3_support: p. 14: "achieves higher EE compared to the convex" optimization is the only non-learned baseline; the only learned comparison is "compared to the PPO approach" (p. 12), i.e. Meta-PPO without its meta-learning module (ablation), and no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the computational complexity for the training mode is given by"; Eqs. (50)-(51) give the training and running complexity orders of Meta-PPO in layer sizes, tasks, episodes and time steps.
q5_support: p. 12: "An ORIS-assisted OWC system is simulated in an indoor"; channels are simulated from the Table II parameters, and the paper gives no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data.
notes: Included as area 3: the learned Meta-PPO policy sets the LED-array precoders and the ORIS element association, together with LED selection and rate adaptation (pp. 8-9). The system is optical wireless (LED and photodiode), not RF, so the reviewer may confirm that the scope admits it. q2: the meta-adaptation phase exists (Algorithm 2) but the results state no unseen test scenario or adaptation effort, so 0; the reviewer may read the meta-learning claim on p. 10 as met. q3: PPO is the proposed method without meta-learning, counted as an ablation; the earlier PPO conference paper [29] by the same authors is cited (p. 2) but not stated as the compared baseline. Table II lists no ORIS element count.
